items.description: A WireGuard instance (VPN → WireGuard → Instances): a local wgN interface. Peers attach themselves with opnsense_wireguard_peer.instance_ids.

privkey.description: Private key. Omit to have the provider generate one (locally, X25519). It is stored in Terraform state, like every OPNsense secret managed by Terraform.

pubkey.description: Public key, derived from private_key. Give it to the peers.

port.description: UDP listen port. Allow it on WAN with a firewall rule.

tunneladdress.description: Instance addresses in CIDR notation, e.g. `10.10.10.1/24`.

disableroutes.description: Do not install routes for the peers' allowed IPs. Set it when routing to networks behind peers with opnsense_gateway and opnsense_route instead.

gateway.description: Gateway IP, for use with disable_routes.

instance.description: The N in wgN, assigned by OPNsense.

interface.description: Device name, e.g. `wg0`. Use it to assign the interface and write firewall rules.

peers.description: Peer UUIDs; change membership through the peers' instance_ids.

carp_depend_on.description: Virtual IP (CARP) this instance follows: it only runs on the CARP master.

items.description: A WireGuard peer (VPN → WireGuard → Peers): a remote device or site.

psk.description: Optional preshared key (`wg genpsk`), for post-quantum resistance.

tunneladdress.description: The peer's allowed IPs in CIDR notation: `10.10.10.2/32` for a single device, or also whole networks behind it for site-to-site, e.g. `["10.20.0.2/32", "192.168.50.0/24"]`.

serveraddress.description: Where the peer is reachable (site-to-site). Omit for road warriors.

servers.description: IDs of the opnsense_wireguard_instance resources this peer belongs to.

privkey.description: The peer's private key, if you want OPNsense to keep it for exporting the peer configuration.
